title: After-action: autosuggest Optimize safe-rollforward, cost-guardrails and rollback orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A config rollout from the Optimize autotuner changed batching and KV-cache settings across a subset of hosted customers. The rollout triggered unexpected KV-warm cache thrashing and an increase in per-token compute for some model sizes, causing a 2.8x cost spike for affected accounts and elevated latency (p95 +120ms) for long-sequence workloads. The automated rollback path did not execute due to a race-condition in the safe-apply orchestrator. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, mitigations deployed, and the longer-term playbook + automation we need to prevent regressions.
impact: Observed cost spikes for ~12% of live traffic routed through Optimize autotuning; three enterprise customers reported increased token billing and latency-sensitive errors that triggered paging. Platform-side SLOs for latency were breached for 40 minutes during peak traffic window.
timeline: 2026-02-28 09:12 UTC - Autotuner job started sweeping conservative->aggressive batching and cache trimming profiles.
2026-02-28 09:37 UTC - First alerts: per-customer cost per token metric (optimize.cost_per_token) increased beyond threshold for two customers.
2026-02-28 09:45 UTC - On-call runbook invoked; attempt to trigger automated rollback failed with 500 from safe-apply orchestrator.
2026-02-28 09:50 UTC - Incident declared; traffic shift started to fallback model variants and traffic-partitioning applied.
2026-02-28 10:05 UTC - Manual rollback completed for autotuner config; metrics began returning to baseline over 20 minutes.
2026-02-28 10:30 UTC - Hotfix roll deployed to add an immediate fail-safe for safe-apply (reject config when dry-run mismatch > 5%).
root_cause: A race-condition in the Optimize safe-apply orchestrator allowed a partially applied config to become active before KV-cache warmups and batching adjustments had stabilized. The autotuner lacked a sufficient dry-run metric comparison for cost proxies (cost_per_token, estimated_gpu_ms). The rollback trigger relied solely on latency SLO breaches and did not consider cost signals, so the automated rollback path did not reach its threshold before manual intervention was required.
mitigations_deployed: Immediate manual rollback of the autotuner config across affected shards (completed 2026-02-28 10:05 UTC).
Hotfix to safe-apply: add validation step to require dry-run metric parity (cost and latency) before commit; reject commits with >5% deviation.
Short-term traffic partitioning to route high-seq workloads to stable model variants for 3 hours post-incident.
Alerting added: optimize.cost_per_token and optimize.estimated_gpu_ms now have automated pager thresholds tied to autotuner rollouts.
Confluence playbook draft published and linked below; ops team trained on manual rollback steps and CLI commands.
playbook_snippet:
Preflight (local/dry-run): redwood optimize apply --profile=<profile> --dry-run --target-shard=<shard>
Verify: optimize.cost_per_token, optimize.estimated_gpu_ms, console.routes.latency.p95 are within expected delta
Canary rollout: apply to 2% traffic for 15m, monitor cost/latency/5xx. If deviation <= 3% continue to 10% for 30m. If deviation > 5% abort and rollback immediately.
Automatic rollback triggers: latency p95 > baseline + 50ms sustained 5m OR cost_per_token > baseline * 1.25 sustained 10m OR error-rate increase > 0.5 percentage point.
Manual rollback CLI: redwood optimize rollback --config-id=<id> --force --reason='cost_regression'
Post-rollback validation: run a dry-warm (prefetch KV keys) then run synthetic requests matching 95th percentile sequence lengths and validate metrics.

ENG-10423: Add cost-proxy metrics into dry-run comparison and gate (owner: Mei Huang, est: 3).
ENG-10424: Build canary-orchestrator service to drive incremental rollouts with automatic binary decisions based on multi-signal thresholds (owner: Priya Rao, est: 8).
ENG-10425: Improve autotuner test-harness to simulate KV-warm behavior across model sizes including cold-start regression tests (owner: Marco Alvarez, est: 5).
ENG-10426: Create an Optimize safety policy in Console to allow admins to pin cost/latency budget per-customer which prevents autotuner from exceeding guardrails (owner: Security & Product, est: 5).

notes: Key learning: cost signals must be first-class rollback criteria for any autotuner that mutates batching/caching. Autotuning that changes cache behavior needs an instrumented warmup window and transactional commit semantics to avoid mixed states. Playbook must be short, prescriptive, and executable by on-call within 10 minutes.
